preamble: Four solutions have definitions suggested by two others

clue.text: Evangelist's working as a lexicographer

parts.note: St John wrote one of the four Gospels, so he is an Evangelist; with the possessive S
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A gospel writer's labours are recast as dictionary-making.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson compiled the great 1755 English dictionary. He is also half of Masters and Johnson, the sex researchers whose stages of response give the puzzle its theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Samuel Johnson is the most famous English dictionary compiler, so a name fits a description of his trade.

clue.text: Blue baby's odd part in oxygen row

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: the first letter sits in an odd position of the word baby's, so this picks it out

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel, a scene

explanation.surface: A baby turns blue during a family argument about oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a baby short of oxygen, but here it means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes or films are indecent, a direct synonym for lewd.

clue.text: Gold vase turned up outside island republic

indicators.note: the reversed vase goes outside, wrapping round the gold
in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an urn is a kind of vase
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A golden vase is upended near an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turned up' reads the vase from bottom to top, giving NRU, which 'outside' wraps round the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny Pacific state, an independent republic on a single island.

clue.text: Partly cover balls on 16

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
16 across is STAGE, and a stage of a race is a lap

explanation.surface: Balls landing on a stage partly hide it.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is cricket's set of six deliveries from one bowler. 'on' places OVER above LAP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Things overlap when one extends over part of another, partly covering it.

clue.text: Sexy and fat: recipe for power

indicators.note: R comes in for P, replacing it

parts.note: paunchy means pot-bellied, fat
P is the physics abbreviation for power
R stands for recipe, the old Latin take on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone is both alluring and overweight, with a formula for strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the P of PAUNCHY for R, the doctor's symbol for 'take' (Latin recipe).
explanation.definitionFit: Raunchy describes something earthy and sexually explicit, a looser synonym for sexy.

clue.text: On 16, suffering with persistent pain — time for hospital

indicators.note: T goes in for H, replacing it

parts.note: to be aching is to suffer a dull persistent pain
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A performer on stage is in pain and needs time in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' changes the H of ACHING to T. 16 is STAGE, so the definition reads 'on stage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone performing on stage is acting, so 'on stage' describes the activity.

clue.text: Deputy feeling less well also, we hear

parts.note: number here is more numb, having less feeling

indicators.note: signals that the word for also is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: A deputy reports feeling unwell, too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeling less well' is a trap: it means having less sensation, NUMB-ER, not being ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command is idiomatically called the number two.

clue.text: Suspend setter? Guilty, by the look of it

definitions.text: Guilty, by the look of it

parts.note: to hang is to suspend
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter is suspended and looks guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the gun dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog expression is shamefaced, the look of someone guilty.

clue.text: Unstable condition of zip, with her chinos badly affected, originally

indicators.note: badly means messed up, so these letters are rearranged
originally points to the opening letter of affected

explanation.surface: A woman's trousers have a faulty zip, leaving her in a shaky state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ZIP HER CHINOS, then 'originally' adds the A of affected.
explanation.definitionFit: Schizophrenia is a serious mental illness, an unstable condition of the mind.

clue.text: Hairy man in the sauna

indicators.note: the man is found inside the words the sauna

explanation.surface: A hirsute fellow sits in the steam room.
explanation.walkthrough: Esau, Jacob's brother in Genesis, is described as a hairy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis calls Esau a hairy man, set against his smooth twin Jacob.

clue.text: 16 1's passion shown by former setter after drinking it

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the setter takes in it, swallowing it

parts.note: cement is a setter, something that sets hard

explanation.surface: An ex-compiler shows passion once a drink is downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is not a crossword compiler but something that sets hard. 16 1 means stage one of Masters and Johnson's model of sexual response.
explanation.definitionFit: Excitement is the first phase in Masters and Johnson's four-stage model, a state of aroused passion.

clue.text: Dodgy 10 out of 10 learner's able to reproduce by pairing up

definitions.text: able to reproduce by pairing up

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: 10 across is ESAU
X is the Roman numeral ten
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A shifty character scores full marks while learning to breed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 10 is the entry at 10 across, the second the Roman numeral; 'out of' just links them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual reproduction needs two parents combining, which is reproducing by pairing up.

clue.text: Suggestion hotel uniform gets done differently

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
U is uniform in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: differently means done in another way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hotel's uniforms get redesigned at someone's suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges DONE as ENDO.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect, usually smutty hint, a kind of suggestion.

clue.text: TV programme producer starts to tackle this one particular odour during intercourse

indicators.note: the starts and odour go inside, during, the intercourse

parts.note: sex is intercourse

indicators.note: the opening letters of each of the next four words are taken

parts.note: BO is body odour

explanation.surface: An absurd boast of tackling a smell mid-coitus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'particular' is one of the four words whose first letters are taken, not a description of the odour; 'during' places the lot inside intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-top box decodes broadcast signals into TV pictures, producing the programmes on screen.

clue.text: Undefined number carried by rail, coming in to a scheduled terminus?

definitions.text: Undefined number carried by rail, coming in to a scheduled terminus?

indicators.note: the railed number enters between the letters of to a

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the number is held inside rail

parts.note: taken as written
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

indicators.note: the terminus is the final letter of scheduled

explanation.surface: An unknown quantity of goods arrives by train at its scheduled end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' makes RAINL; 'coming in' puts that inside TOA; 'terminus' adds the D ending scheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainload is however much one train carries to its destination.

clue.text: Put on Men Only revue at last

parts.note: a stag do is for men only

indicators.note: points to the final letter of revue

explanation.surface: A men-only revue is finally mounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men Only' was also a British magazine, adding to the smutty theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a show is to put it on in a theatre.

clue.text: Childless set spread out

parts.note: s.p. is the genealogists' sine prole, without issue
to set down is to lay

explanation.surface: A childless couple's arrangement spreads apart.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole, Latin for 'without offspring') appears in family trees and Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: To splay is to spread out, like fingers or legs.

clue.text: 16 2's high-level flat Paul cooked meal in

indicators.note: the meal goes inside the rearranged name
cooked means doctored, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
tea is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Paul cooks a meal in his upstairs flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the name to PLAU before the meal goes in. Stage two in Masters and Johnson's model is the plateau phase.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a raised level tract of land, and also the second phase of sexual response.

clue.text: Most orchards (more than half) rent spaces online

indicators.note: rent here is torn apart, so these letters are scrambled
the first five of the eight letters of orchards are kept

explanation.surface: Most orchards are leased out as spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is the past tense of rend, not a payment; it shuffles MOST and ORCHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatrooms are areas on the internet where users talk in real time.

clue.text: Severely punish counter-revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning things round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to crack down on counter-revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat or chastise heavily, so to punish severely.

clue.text: Gets to grips with maiden's top and bloomers

indicators.note: the top of a down entry word is its first letter

parts.note: asters are flowers, things that bloom

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a maiden's top and undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' are not knickers but plants that bloom. Masters partners Johnson (1 across) in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to get to grips with it.

clue.text: Doctor is sued for neglect

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor is taken to court for negligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the defendant but is a verb signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of being no longer used, neglect.

clue.text: Intravenously inject drug that has mother-in-law, not a wife, in ecstasy

indicators.note: the a and the wife are left out

parts.note: mother is MA, then IN, and law is LAW
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug user's mother-in-law, not his wife, is high on ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops A and W from LAW, leaving MAINL.
explanation.definitionFit: To mainline is slang for injecting a drug straight into a vein.

clue.text: 16 3's earth mover, perhaps, for gas main's housing

indicators.note: the words for gas main's hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: An excavator housed near a gas main.
explanation.walkthrough: Stage three in Masters and Johnson's model. 'Earth mover' plays on the joke 'did the earth move for you?'
explanation.definitionFit: Climax is stage three of the sexual response model, jokingly what makes the earth move.

clue.text: Outcry as organ explodes

indicators.note: something that explodes is blown apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shout goes up as the church organ blows up.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a cry of pain or protest, a kind of outcry.

clue.text: 16 4's determination to get fifth letter in right answer

parts.note: E is the fifth letter of the alphabet
a solution is an answer

explanation.surface: A resolve to slot the letter E into the right answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Stage four in Masters and Johnson's model is the resolution phase.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution means firm resolve, and also the final phase of sexual response.

clue.text: Hen party's warning sign?

parts.note: a hen party has zero, O, of the next piece
a hen party has no males, men

explanation.surface: Is a hen party a bad sign?
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a bride's pre-wedding night out with female friends, so it has 'O men'.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign warning of things to come.

clue.text: Number cruncher's tip

parts.note: the first letter of cruncher is C, the Roman numeral for this number

explanation.surface: Advice from an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number cruncher' wants to be an accountant; read 'Number' alone as the definition, and the tip of 'cruncher' is C, Roman for it.
explanation.definitionFit: C is the Roman numeral meaning one hundred, the number the clue points to.

clue.text: Quality of water nurse added into stew on return

indicators.note: the whole is then read backwards
the nurse goes inside the stew

parts.note: taken as written
SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse adds water to a stew on coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'added into' gives SSENTEW; 'on return' turns it to WETNESS. SEN was a grade of British nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Wetness is the defining property of water, its quality of being wet.
